lessons.title: Calling the Play
lessons.blurb: The huddle, the clock and the last minutes.

steps.title: The play call
steps.body: Before each play, the coach picks a play and the quarterback tells the team in the huddle. That's the play call. It says the formation and what each player does.

steps.prompt: Who usually picks the play before the snap?
choices: The coach, and the quarterback tells the team
steps.explanation: Yes. The coach sends in the call, and the quarterback calls it in the huddle.

steps.title: The play clock
steps.body: After each play, the offense has 40 seconds to snap the ball. A play clock counts down. If it reaches zero first, that's delay of game.

steps.statement: If the play clock reaches zero before the snap, the offense gets a penalty.
steps.explanation: Yes. Delay of game costs 5 yards.

steps.title: The two-minute warning
steps.body: In the NFL, when two minutes are left in each half, the clock stops for the two-minute warning. Teams use the break to plan their last plays.

steps.prompt: When does the two-minute warning happen?
choices: With 2 minutes left in each half
At the start of the game
When a team has 2 timeouts left
steps.explanation: Yes. It happens near the end of the first half and the end of the game.

steps.title: Spike and kneel
steps.body: To stop the clock fast, the quarterback can spike the ball into the ground right after the snap. To let the clock run, a team that is winning has the quarterback kneel down.

steps.prompt: Your team is behind with 10 seconds left, the clock is running and you have no timeouts. How can you stop the clock?
steps.explanation: Yes. A spike is an incomplete pass on purpose, so the clock stops. It uses up a down.

steps.prompt: Your team is winning near the end, and the other team has no timeouts. What can the quarterback do to run out the clock?
steps.explanation: Yes. He kneels, the play ends safely, and the clock keeps running.

lessons.title: Replay and Overtime
lessons.blurb: Checking the call, and breaking a tie.

steps.title: Replay
steps.body: Officials can watch a video replay to check a call. In the NFL, every score and every turnover is checked.

steps.title: The red flag
steps.body: An NFL coach who thinks a call was wrong can throw a red flag to challenge it. If the call stands, his team loses a timeout.

steps.prompt: A coach throws a red flag onto the field. What does he want?
choices: The officials to check the call on replay
A penalty on his own team
steps.explanation: Yes. That's a challenge. The officials look at the replay and decide.

steps.statement: Officials can use video replay to check whether a touchdown really was a touchdown.
steps.explanation: Yes. In the NFL every scoring play is reviewed.

steps.title: Overtime
steps.body: If the score is tied when the fourth quarter ends, the game goes to overtime: an extra period to find a winner.

steps.prompt: The score is tied when the fourth quarter ends. What happens next in the NFL?
choices: The game is replayed next week
steps.explanation: Yes. Both teams get a chance to score in overtime. In the regular season it can still end in a tie.
